issue.title: sase-core flake: agent_scan query_cache identical_revalidate_is_cheaper_than_cold_decode inverts its single-sample wall-clock timing under full-gate load
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-1vn.4.1.1 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1) of epic sase-1vn.4.1; filed by the sase-1vn.4.1 land agent.

During the sase-1vn.4.1.1 detection phase (2026-11-27, sase-core tree based on 34461b7f), `sase tool run check` in sase-core failed only this node: cold 347 ms, warm 781 ms, so `assert!(warm < cold)` fired. The test source is unchanged since de476054/575d4300/102b009d (2026-11-23), and the phase's diff did not touch agent_scan. An isolated rerun passed in 0.20 s. Observed fail rate: 1 of 2 runs (1 parallel full-gate failure, 1 isolated pass); it did not reproduce serially.

Likely root cause: the test compares two single-sample wall-clock timings (`Instant::now()` around one `query_snapshot` call each) inside the parallel full gate, so host contention during the warm sample can invert the order even though the deterministic decode-count assertions (`record_json_decoded == 40` then `== 0`) held. Fix the timing comparison so it is robust to contention (for example min-of-N samples, or keep the decode-count proof as the contract and move the wall-clock ratio to a benchmark). Do not just delete or weaken the cost property without keeping an equivalent proof.
